Running the browser suite in this pod: make a database of your own (`createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U legion_test e2e_<stamp>`) and point DATABASE_URL at it, since the suite resets what it is given; `bunx playwright install chromium` with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH left unset; `cd packages/contracts && bun run build` first, because Playwright resolves @legion/contracts through Node's conditions and reads dist/; and put packages/dispatch/node_modules/.bin on PATH, since e2e/run.ts spawns a bare `playwright`. Rebuild web/dist after every web/src edit: the rows serve the build, not the sources.

The one Playwright argument order that works is `playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts <spec> --project chromium`: a spec written after --project is read as a second project name and the run dies with 'Project(s) ... not found'.

D1's route is `path="/credentials/*"`, not the spec's literal `/credentials/:recordId`, because A5's grep forbids that string in app.tsx and e2e/two-builds-routes.ts. Rendering InboxPage under a second route made routeIsInbox wrong for that path, which the simplify pass caught: the shell decided the viewport and the peek-at-the-inbox drawer from it. routeIsInbox now matches the splat and excludes /credentials/machine, with a test.

The broker's and Dispatch's Go suites need a database of your own too: the pod's server refuses `create schema` in the shared `postgres` database (permission denied for database postgres), so BROKER_TEST_DATABASE_URL and DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL point at postgres://legion_test@127.0.0.1:5433/infra879_impl?sslmode=disable here.
